assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible and is now a standard transformation in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. The discovery is original in its ligand-design logic, clear in what was achieved, and has had very broad, lasting impact. It sits naturally beside the 2010 cross-coupling prize as a conceptually distinct extension.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination with successive ligand generations and mechanistic work. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is an acknowledged precursor and is the main complication, but the decisive general, practical methodology is credited to the two.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Weight to give Kosugi/Migita precedent versus the later general catalytic method
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members hesitant

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological N2 fixation, and its FeMo-cofactor is among the most remarkable metal clusters in nature. Crystal structures of the FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide, and later work on turnover states and cryo-EM of intermediates are structurally rigorous and fundamental to bioinorganic chemistry. Importance is high and the structural evidence is concrete.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the decisive crystallographic structures (cofactor architecture, central carbide, high-resolution states). Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism and biochemistry, and Ribbe cofactor biosynthesis. A fair three-person split is possible but some credit must be left aside.
assessment.maturity: Structures reproduced independently over decades; the catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding site are still only partly resolved, so recognition would be for the structure and framework rather than a closed mechanism.
uncertainties: Whether the mechanism is mature enough for recognition
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe
Nature of the interstitial atom was established late (2011) and cofactor states are still being revised

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaics from a dye-sensitized curiosity to over 25 percent efficiency in about a decade, with a very large community and new defect-tolerant semiconductor chemistry. The materials-chemistry impact is major and original. As a structural chemist I value that the compositional tuneability follows from the perovskite framework.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park the first solid-state cell, and Snaith the efficient planar and mesostructured devices; Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok also made major contributions. Any three-person selection is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Rapid confirmation worldwide, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial deployment are not settled, so recognition may be somewhat early. The chemistry of degradation and the best compositions is still evolving.
uncertainties: Contested credit among six or more leading figures
Stability and commercial viability not demonstrated at scale
Whether the committee sees it as primarily physics or device engineering

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, such as photosystem II and photoactive proteins, before radiation damage. It is an enabling method that opens structural work on samples not accessible to conventional crystallography, which I find compelling. Originality and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Chapman and collaborators (including Hajdu through the diffract-before-destroy concept) established the principle and early demonstrations; Fromme and Schlichting contributed key biological applications and methods. Allocation among Hajdu, Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting is difficult, and the concept predates the experiments.
assessment.maturity: Proof of principle was shown in 2009-2011, and the method is now widely used, but dependence on large facilities and the modest number of landmark structures argue that impact is still maturing. Complementary micro-crystal electron diffraction and synchrotron serial methods compete for the same niche.
uncertainties: Whether the lasting impact will match the facility investment
Role of Hajdu in attribution and the concept versus the experimental demonstration
Competition from micro-ED and serial synchrotron crystallography

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of two-dimensional transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases. They show tunable composition and surface terminations and are studied for energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. This is a clear new materials class with a structurally defined discovery, which is the kind of inorganic and materials chemistry I follow closely.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum produced and developed the first Ti3C2 MXene (2011). Barsoum's MAX phase background and Gogotsi's leadership of the field give a natural three-person credit, although others have also driven applications.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years of strong independent confirmation and rapid growth, but practical applications and technological use are still emerging. Recognition might be early.
uncertainties: Application impact is not yet proven
Surface termination and structural characterisation can be complex and sample dependent
Role of Naguib relative to the senior authors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cell combined high-surface-area mesoporous TiO2 with molecular sensitizers and a redox electrolyte, creating a new route to photovoltaics and a major field in molecular and materials photochemistry. Originality and lasting influence, including the later link to perovskite cells, are strong.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the defining work; Grätzel is the clear central figure. Hagfeldt's contribution is as a long-term developer rather than a co-discoverer, so a two-person credit may be more natural.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades with commercial niches, but efficiency has been overtaken by perovskite and silicon cells and commercial impact is limited, so the recognition case rests on conceptual and scientific importance.
uncertainties: Limited commercial success compared with initial promise
Whether Hagfeldt belongs in a prize configuration
Dependence on how the committee views the perovskite candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near-quantum accuracy at near-force-field cost and are transforming molecular simulation of materials and reactions. Neural-network (Behler-Parrinello) and Gaussian-approximation potentials are conceptually original and broadly adopted in materials chemistry, which is important for the structure and function questions I care about.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello (2007) introduced high-dimensional neural-network potentials, while Bartók and Csányi introduced Gaussian-approximation potentials. Many others (E, von Lilienfeld) are credited, so a fair three-person split is arguable. Parrinello also appears in other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving field with strong uptake, but transferability, reliability and generalization limits remain; foundation models are changing the landscape. Possibly premature.
uncertainties: Premature while the methodology is still evolving rapidly
Many contributors and overlap with other computational candidates
Whether the 2024 prize for AI-based protein structure prediction affects appetite for a further computation-driven prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, especially reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis (Solexa/Illumina chemistry), reduced the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude and changed biology and medicine. Its impact is among the largest in recent chemistry-enabled technology, and it was a chemical invention in its nucleotide and surface chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry, and Mayer contributed an early parallel clustering concept. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, Ion Torrent) and Ju (reversible terminators) lead competing routes, so credit is divided between technologies and the sequencing field has several legitimate claimants.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and universally used, so timing is unquestionable. The attribution problem is the dominant uncertainty.
uncertainties: Disputed allocation across competing sequencing technologies
Whether the committee regards it as chemistry or physiology/medicine
Role of Mayer and Ju in a final configuration
